My comeback story

Some journeys begin with a dream. Mine began in 6th grade, with a throwball in my hands and a love for the game that I never knew would take me this far.

Hi, I’m Kaaviya Murugesan, from Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. What started as a school sport in India slowly became my passion, my happiness, and a huge part of who I am.

From sub-junior to junior and senior tournaments, I represented my district and state, played in more than 100 tournaments, won many competitions, and received the Most Valuable Player (MVP) award. Throwball was never just about winning. It was the excitement of stepping onto the court, the bond with my teammates, and giving everything I had for the game.

Then, as I started building my career, I had to take a break. Walking away from something I loved was not easy. But some passions never really leave you.

Moving to Pittsburgh gave me a fresh start, and I found my way back to the court. I started playing again, traveling across the United States for tournaments, meeting new teammates, and challenging myself all over again.

Now I have been selected to represent the USA Women’s National Team at an international competition in India on December 28–29, 2026. The girl who started in 6th grade in India is getting the chance to play for the United States on an international stage.

It reminds me that taking a break does not mean giving up, and that it is never too late to chase something you truly love.

This is my story. This is my comeback. And this is only the beginning.
